**Verdict: hold until one line is changed.**

**Claims list**

| Claim | Status |
|---|---|
| "the Christmas blend is back" | Allowed (product facts, new arrivals) |
| "Black tea, orange peel, cinnamon and a little clove" | Allowed (ingredients) |
| "back in the shop from today" | Allowed (availability), assuming it is true for today's send |
| "selling fast" | **Unsupported.** It implies scarcity and demand with no verifiable figure behind it, so it counts as fake urgency. |

**Slop check:** There are no banned words, no em-dash sandwiches, no exclamation points, no rhetorical opener and no invented stats. The opener "Quick one this week" is mild throat-clearing, but it is short and fine to keep.

**Fix:** Cut "selling fast". If you want urgency, it has to be real and checkable, such as a limited batch size or a stock level. I've left a placeholder for that.

**Suggested version:**

> Quick one this week: the Christmas blend is back. Black tea, orange peel, cinnamon and a little clove. It's in the shop from today.
>
> [PROOF NEEDED: if the batch is genuinely limited, state the real quantity or stock status]
